#!/bin/zsh
# usage: q.sh artemis|aurora|pulse < query.sql   (pipes the runner via stdin; no files written in the pod)
export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH
K=(kubectl --context prod -n duploservices-prod --request-timeout=120s)
Q=$(base64 | tr -d '\n')
case $1 in
  artemis) "${K[@]}" exec -i deploy/artemis -c artemis -- env Q=$Q H=duploartemis-prod-v2-replica.c8da0aw2akcu.us-east-1.rds.amazonaws.com python - < /tmp/wevo-ft-scope/runpy.py ;;
  pulse)   "${K[@]}" exec -i deploy/personas-api -c personas-api -- env Q=$Q RLS_BYPASS=1 /app/.venv/bin/python - < /tmp/wevo-ft-scope/runpy.py ;;
  aurora)  "${K[@]}" exec -i deploy/customer-api -c customer-api -- env Q=$Q NODE_PATH=/wevo/app/node_modules node - < /tmp/wevo-ft-scope/runnode.js ;;
esac
---RUNPY
# Runs ONE read-only aggregate SELECT from stdin. Env: H (host override), plus pod DB_* env.
import os, sys, re, time, psycopg2
import base64; sql = base64.b64decode(os.environ["Q"]).decode().strip().rstrip(";")
body = re.sub(r'--[^\n]*', '', sql).strip().lower()
assert body.startswith(('select', 'with', 'explain')), 'only SELECT/WITH allowed'
assert ';' not in body, 'single statement only'
for w in ('insert ', 'update ', 'delete ', 'drop ', 'alter ', 'create ', 'truncate ', 'grant ', 'copy '):
    assert w not in body, 'forbidden keyword ' + w
kw = dict(host=os.environ.get('H') or os.environ['DB_HOST'], port=os.environ.get('DB_PORT', 5432),
          dbname=os.environ['DB_NAME'], user=os.environ['DB_USER'], password=os.environ['DB_PASSWORD'],
          connect_timeout=15, application_name='ft-scope-readonly-aggregate')
if os.environ.get('DB_SSLMODE'):
    kw['sslmode'] = os.environ['DB_SSLMODE']
    if kw['sslmode'] == 'verify-full':
        kw['sslrootcert'] = os.environ.get('CA_PEM_PATH', '/etc/ssl/certs/global-bundle.pem')
c = psycopg2.connect(**kw)
cur = c.cursor()
cur.execute("SET default_transaction_read_only = on")
cur.execute("SET statement_timeout = '60s'")
cur.execute("SET lock_timeout = '5s'")
if os.environ.get('RLS_BYPASS'):
    cur.execute("SET app.is_service_role = 'true'")
cur.execute("BEGIN READ ONLY")
cur.execute("SELECT inet_server_addr()::text, pg_is_in_recovery(), current_setting('transaction_read_only')")
print('# server', cur.fetchone()[1:], file=sys.stderr)
t = time.time(); cur.execute(sql)
print('\t'.join(d[0] for d in cur.description))
for r in cur.fetchall():
    print('\t'.join('' if v is None else str(v) for v in r))
cur.execute("ROLLBACK"); c.close()
print('# %.1fs' % (time.time() - t), file=sys.stderr)
---RUNNODE
// Runs ONE read-only aggregate SELECT from env Q (base64) against Aurora using pod POSTGRES_* env.
const { Client } = require('pg');
const sql = Buffer.from(process.env.Q, 'base64').toString().trim().replace(/;\s*$/, '');
const body = sql.replace(/--[^\n]*/g, '').trim().toLowerCase();
if (!/^(select|with|explain)/.test(body) || body.includes(';')) throw new Error('only single SELECT/WITH');
for (const w of ['insert ', 'update ', 'delete ', 'drop ', 'alter ', 'create ', 'truncate ', 'grant ', 'copy '])
  if (body.includes(w)) throw new Error('forbidden ' + w);
(async () => {
  const e = process.env;
  const c = new Client({ host: e.POSTGRES_HOST, port: e.POSTGRES_PORT || 5432, database: e.POSTGRES_DATABASE,
    user: e.POSTGRES_USER || 'wevo_admin', password: e.POSTGRES_PASSWORD, ssl: { rejectUnauthorized: false },
    connectionTimeoutMillis: 15000, application_name: 'ft-scope-readonly-aggregate' });
  await c.connect();
  await c.query("SET default_transaction_read_only = on");
  await c.query("SET statement_timeout = '60s'");
  await c.query("SET lock_timeout = '5s'");
  await c.query('BEGIN READ ONLY');
  const s = await c.query("select pg_is_in_recovery() r, current_setting('transaction_read_only') ro");
  console.error('# server', JSON.stringify(s.rows[0]));
  const t = Date.now(); const r = await c.query(sql);
  console.log(r.fields.map(f => f.name).join('\t'));
  for (const row of r.rows) console.log(r.fields.map(f => row[f.name] == null ? '' : String(row[f.name])).join('\t'));
  await c.query('ROLLBACK'); await c.end();
  console.error('# ' + ((Date.now() - t) / 1000).toFixed(1) + 's');
})().catch(err => { console.error('ERR', err.message); process.exit(1); });
---C1
-- Exact cohort source join from customer-api src/data/pulseTags.js _getTagQuantData, aggregated per distinct pulse
with rows_ as (
  select pt.id as tag_id, pt.type as tag_type, ptt.pulse_id, aisr.id as result_id, aisr.created_at,
         (aisr.quant->'scores'->0->>'score') ~ '^-?[0-9.]+$' and (aisr.quant->'scores'->1->>'score') ~ '^-?[0-9.]+$'
           and (aisr.quant->'scores'->2->>'score') ~ '^-?[0-9.]+$' and (aisr.quant->>'average') ~ '^-?[0-9.]+$' as complete,
         (aisr.quant->'scores'->0->>'name') in ('Intuitive','Trusted','Valuable') and (aisr.quant->'scores'->1->>'name') in ('Intuitive','Trusted','Valuable')
           and (aisr.quant->'scores'->2->>'name') in ('Intuitive','Trusted','Valuable') as names_ok
  from wevo.pulse_to_tag ptt
  join wevo.pulse_tag pt on pt.id = ptt.tag_id
  join wevo.automated_insight_session_result aisr on aisr.automated_insight_session_id = ptt.pulse_id
  where ptt.deleted_at is null and aisr.quant <> '{}' and aisr.segment_id is null and pt.is_active is true),
per_pulse as (
  select pulse_id, max(created_at) as created_at, count(distinct result_id) as n_results,
         count(distinct tag_type) as n_types, bool_and(complete) as complete, bool_and(names_ok) as names_ok
  from rows_ group by pulse_id)
select to_char(date_trunc('month',created_at),'YYYY-MM') as month,
       count(*) as n_pulses, sum(n_results) as n_result_rows,
       count(*) filter (where n_types=3) as n_all3_types, count(*) filter (where n_types=2) as n_2_types, count(*) filter (where n_types=1) as n_1_type,
       count(*) filter (where complete) as n_complete_scores, count(*) filter (where not names_ok) as n_names_not_itv,
       count(*) filter (where n_results>1) as n_multi_result
from per_pulse group by rollup(1) order by 1 nulls last
---C2
with rows_ as (
  select pt.id as tag_id, pt.type as tag_type, ptt.pulse_id, aisr.created_at,
         (aisr.quant->'scores'->0->>'score') ~ '^-?[0-9.]+$' and (aisr.quant->'scores'->1->>'score') ~ '^-?[0-9.]+$'
           and (aisr.quant->'scores'->2->>'score') ~ '^-?[0-9.]+$' and (aisr.quant->>'average') ~ '^-?[0-9.]+$' as complete
  from wevo.pulse_to_tag ptt
  join wevo.pulse_tag pt on pt.id = ptt.tag_id
  join wevo.automated_insight_session_result aisr on aisr.automated_insight_session_id = ptt.pulse_id
  where ptt.deleted_at is null and aisr.quant <> '{}' and aisr.segment_id is null and pt.is_active is true),
per_pulse as (
  select pulse_id,
         max(tag_id::text) filter (where tag_type='product') as p,
         max(tag_id::text) filter (where tag_type='industry') as i,
         max(tag_id::text) filter (where tag_type='asset') as a
  from rows_ group by pulse_id having bool_and(complete)),
combos as (
  select 'global' as kind, 'global' as key from per_pulse
  union all select 'product', p from per_pulse where p is not null
  union all select 'industry', i from per_pulse where i is not null
  union all select 'asset', a from per_pulse where a is not null
  union all select 'product_industry', p||'_'||i from per_pulse where p is not null and i is not null
  union all select 'product_asset', p||'_'||a from per_pulse where p is not null and a is not null
  union all select 'industry_asset', i||'_'||a from per_pulse where i is not null and a is not null
  union all select 'product_industry_asset', p||'_'||i||'_'||a from per_pulse where p is not null and i is not null and a is not null),
sizes as (select kind, key, count(*) as n from combos group by kind, key)
select kind, count(*) as n_cohorts, count(*) filter (where n>=10) as n_cohorts_ge10,
       sum(n) as n_memberships,
       percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by n) as p50_size, percentile_cont(0.9) within group (order by n) as p90_size,
       percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by n) filter (where n>=10) as p50_size_ge10, max(n) as max_size
from sizes group by kind
order by case kind when 'global' then 0 when 'product' then 1 when 'industry' then 2 when 'asset' then 3 when 'product_industry' then 4 when 'product_asset' then 5 when 'industry_asset' then 6 else 7 end
---T1
-- Artemis pulse_tag: counts by type/active, embedding shape (aggregates only)
select type,
       count(*) as n_total,
       count(*) filter (where is_active and deleted_at is null) as n_active,
       count(*) filter (where deleted_at is not null) as n_deleted,
       count(*) filter (where embedding is not null and jsonb_typeof(embedding)='array' and jsonb_array_length(embedding)>0) as n_with_embedding,
       min(jsonb_array_length(embedding)) filter (where jsonb_typeof(embedding)='array') as emb_dim_min,
       max(jsonb_array_length(embedding)) filter (where jsonb_typeof(embedding)='array') as emb_dim_max,
       percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by octet_length(embedding::text)) as emb_text_bytes_p50,
       max(octet_length(embedding::text)) as emb_text_bytes_max,
       percentile_cont(0.5) within group (order by octet_length(coalesce(name,''))+octet_length(coalesce(description,''))) as name_desc_bytes_p50,
       max(octet_length(coalesce(name,''))+octet_length(coalesce(description,''))) as name_desc_bytes_max,
       min(created_at)::date as first_created, max(created_at)::date as last_created, max(updated_at)::date as last_updated
from wevo.pulse_tag
group by rollup(type) order by 1 nulls last
---T7
select c.relname, c.reltuples::bigint as est_rows, pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(c.oid)) as total_size,
       (select string_agg(a.attname||':'||format_type(a.atttypid,a.atttypmod), ', ' order by a.attnum)
          from pg_attribute a where a.attrelid=c.oid and a.attnum>0 and not a.attisdropped) as cols
from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid=c.relnamespace
where n.nspname='wevo' and c.relkind='r' and (c.relname in ('pulse_benchmark','automated_insight_session_result','automated_insight_session') or c.relname like '%benchmark%' or c.relname like '%quant%')
order by 1
---T9
select c.relname, c.reltuples::bigint as est_rows,
       pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(c.oid)) as heap_only, pg_size_pretty(pg_indexes_size(c.oid)) as indexes,
       pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(c.oid) - pg_relation_size(c.oid) - pg_indexes_size(c.oid)) as toast,
       (select pg_size_pretty(avg_width::bigint) from pg_stats s where s.schemaname='wevo' and s.tablename=c.relname and s.attname='quant') as quant_avg_width,
       (select null_frac from pg_stats s where s.schemaname='wevo' and s.tablename=c.relname and s.attname='quant') as quant_null_frac
from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid=c.relnamespace
where n.nspname='wevo' and c.relname in ('automated_insight_session_result','automated_insight_session','pulse_to_tag','pulse_tag') order by 1
---A5
select tablename, indexname, indexdef from pg_indexes where schemaname='wevo' and tablename in ('pulse_benchmark','pulse_to_tag','pulse_tag') order by 1,2

---
name: prod-db-query-load-rules
description: "Ryan's rule (2026-11-03) for read-only scoping queries against live production databases - Artemis replica for anything heavy, Aurora catalog-only, CloudWatch CPU gate"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 145e7c3a-80db-4502-9e1c-b5431f5b554d
  modified: 2026-11-03T20:34:05.147Z
---

Ryan stopped a scoping session mid-run on 2026-11-03 because aggregate queries were hitting live production databases. Rules given:

- Use the Artemis read replica (`duploartemis-prod-v2-replica`, via `deploy/artemis`) for every table that exists there.
- Aurora (`duplowevo-db`, db.t3.medium, no replica) gets only cheap catalog queries (`pg_class.reltuples`, `pg_total_relation_size`, `pg_indexes`) and small indexed COUNTs on `pulse_tag` / `pulse_to_tag`. Never detoast `automated_insight_session_result.quant` on Aurora and never run a full-table GROUP BY over it. `pulse_benchmark` has only a primary-key index, so per-month counts on it are also off limits.
- Before any non-trivial query, check CloudWatch `AWS/RDS CPUUtilization` for the target instance with the read-only profile `duplo.argus.wevo.ai` (region us-east-1 for RDS/CloudWatch). Skip the query if CPU is over 50%.
- Pulse_db (`duplopersonas-prod`) has no replica either.

**Why:** these are the live customer databases; a 5 s quant scan on the Aurora t3.medium competes with customer traffic. When cohort sizes need quant presence and the data is not on the replica, estimate from catalog stats plus earlier counts and label it an estimate.

**How to apply:** wrap every pod-exec query in the CPU gate first, pick the replica by default, and treat Aurora as catalog-only unless the count is on a small indexed table. The guarded runner is `/tmp/wevo-ft-scope/q.sh`. See [[wevo-prod-readonly-data-access]] and [[pulse-benchmark-cohort-and-tag-catalog-2026-11]].

------
---
name: pulse-benchmark-cohort-and-tag-catalog-2026-11
description: "Where Pulse tag catalog embeddings and benchmark cohort data live, their measured sizes (2026-11-03), and the fact that native Pulses never feed back into the Aurora benchmark cohort"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: da89655d-caa3-4e6c-a5c9-959473d3008a
  modified: 2026-11-03T20:24:04.021Z
---

Measured read-only on prod 2026-11-03 (aggregate queries at `/tmp/wevo-tag-scope/*.sql`, runner `/tmp/wevo-ft-scope/q.sh`):

- Two `wevo.pulse_tag` tables. Only the **Artemis** copy has `embedding` (jsonb array, 3072 floats, `text-embedding-3-large`), `description`, `notes`; Aurora's copy is id/type/name/is_active only. Both: 185 tags (157 product, 14 industry, 14 asset), all active, all created 2024-08-07, never updated or deleted since. Artemis table 7.5 MB, embedding JSON text ~68.9 KB per tag.
- Benchmark cohort source is `_getTagQuantData` in `wevo-customer-api/src/data/pulseTags.js` (Aurora: pulse_to_tag × pulse_tag × automated_insight_session_result, `segment_id is null`, `quant <> '{}'`), cached in-process 1 h. Cohort = 28,834 pulses, all with numeric I/T/V/average; 69% have all three tag types. ~21.6k (75%) predate 2024-11-18 and get the Box-Cox rescale at read time.
- `wevo.pulse_benchmark` (97 MB, 65k rows / 32k active) IS read back at runtime via `getSanitizedBenchmarks` from `query.js` for legacy report views; `runPulseLegacyBenchmarks` (native Pulses) only computes and writes nothing to Aurora.
- **Native wevo-pulse Pulses never join the cohort**: Aurora stopped getting scored pulses in the week of 2026-10-05 (0/week since) while pulse_db native sessions with quant run 35–120/week. The cohort is frozen at ~28.8k unless Pulse writes native scores back.
- Compact JSON of the cohort measured at 6.2 MB with UUIDs (~216 B/pulse); catalog JSON ≈ 13 MB (2.3 MB as float32).
- Governance: no doc restricts copying; `docs/pulse-report-provenance-map.md` calls the taxonomy and corpus WEVO IP; data-deletion template (`db-migrations/data_deletion`) deletes pulse_to_tag/pulse_benchmark rows, so a snapshot must be refreshed after deletion runs. No CODEOWNERS anywhere.

**Why:** needed to pick where Pulse keeps offline reference data for quant/tag/benchmark independence from customer-api and Artemis.
**How to apply:** scope any benchmark snapshot from Aurora, embeddings from Artemis; treat growth as ~0/week until native write-back exists. See [[wevo-prod-readonly-data-access]] and [[pulse-usage-reporting-data-map]].

name: wevo-prod-access-and-topology
description: How to inspect WEVO Pulse/customer-app production and stage read-only (AWS profiles, kube contexts, CLIs, hostnames, deploy workflows)
metadata:
  type: reference
---

- Shell PATH in this harness is minimal; CLIs live in `/opt/homebrew/bin` (aws, gh, terraform, auth0, uv, node) and `/usr/local/bin/kubectl`. There is no global `yarn`; wevo-access (node ^22, yarn 3.6.4 via packageManager) needs `PATH=$HOME/.nvm/versions/node/v22.22.0/bin:$PATH COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0` so its husky pre-commit (`yarn lint-staged` + `make code-quality`, ~3 min) can run instead of being bypassed.

name: prod-db-query-load-rules
description: "Ryan's rule (2026-11-03) for read-only scoping queries against live production databases - Artemis replica for anything heavy, Aurora catalog-only, CloudWatch CPU gate"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 145e7c3a-80db-4502-9e1c-b5431f5b554d
  modified: 2026-11-03T20:34:05.147Z
---

Ryan stopped a scoping session mid-run on 2026-11-03 because aggregate queries were hitting live production databases. Rules given:

- Use the Artemis read replica (`duploartemis-prod-v2-replica`, via `deploy/artemis`) for every table that exists there.
- Aurora (`duplowevo-db`, db.t3.medium, no replica) gets only cheap catalog queries (`pg_class.reltuples`, `pg_total_relation_size`, `pg_indexes`) and small indexed COUNTs on `pulse_tag` / `pulse_to_tag`. Never detoast `automated_insight_session_result.quant` on Aurora and never run a full-table GROUP BY over it. `pulse_benchmark` has only a primary-key index, so per-month counts on it are also off limits.
- Before any non-trivial query, check CloudWatch `AWS/RDS CPUUtilization` for the target instance with the read-only profile `duplo.argus.wevo.ai` (region us-east-1 for RDS/CloudWatch). Skip the query if CPU is over 50%.
- Pulse_db (`duplopersonas-prod`) has no replica either.

**Why:** these are the live customer databases; a 5 s quant scan on the Aurora t3.medium competes with customer traffic. When cohort sizes need quant presence and the data is not on the replica, estimate from catalog stats plus earlier counts and label it an estimate.

**How to apply:** wrap every pod-exec query in the CPU gate first, pick the replica by default, and treat Aurora as catalog-only unless the count is on a small indexed table. The guarded runner is `/tmp/wevo-ft-scope/q.sh`. See [[wevo-prod-readonly-data-access]] and [[pulse-benchmark-cohort-and-tag-catalog-2026-11]].

---
name: pulse-benchmark-cohort-and-tag-catalog-2026-11
description: "Where Pulse tag catalog embeddings and benchmark cohort data live, their measured sizes (2026-11-03), and the fact that native Pulses never feed back into the Aurora benchmark cohort"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: da89655d-caa3-4e6c-a5c9-959473d3008a
  modified: 2026-11-03T20:24:04.021Z
---

Measured read-only on prod 2026-11-03 (aggregate queries at `/tmp/wevo-tag-scope/*.sql`, runner `/tmp/wevo-ft-scope/q.sh`):

- Two `wevo.pulse_tag` tables. Only the **Artemis** copy has `embedding` (jsonb array, 3072 floats, `text-embedding-3-large`), `description`, `notes`; Aurora's copy is id/type/name/is_active only. Both: 185 tags (157 product, 14 industry, 14 asset), all active, all created 2024-08-07, never updated or deleted since. Artemis table 7.5 MB, embedding JSON text ~68.9 KB per tag.
- Benchmark cohort source is `_getTagQuantData` in `wevo-customer-api/src/data/pulseTags.js` (Aurora: pulse_to_tag × pulse_tag × automated_insight_session_result, `segment_id is null`, `quant <> '{}'`), cached in-process 1 h. Cohort = 28,834 pulses, all with numeric I/T/V/average; 69% have all three tag types. ~21.6k (75%) predate 2024-11-18 and get the Box-Cox rescale at read time.
- `wevo.pulse_benchmark` (97 MB, 65k rows / 32k active) IS read back at runtime via `getSanitizedBenchmarks` from `query.js` for legacy report views; `runPulseLegacyBenchmarks` (native Pulses) only computes and writes nothing to Aurora.
- **Native wevo-pulse Pulses never join the cohort**: Aurora stopped getting scored pulses in the week of 2026-10-05 (0/week since) while pulse_db native sessions with quant run 35–120/week. The cohort is frozen at ~28.8k unless Pulse writes native scores back.
- Compact JSON of the cohort measured at 6.2 MB with UUIDs (~216 B/pulse); catalog JSON ≈ 13 MB (2.3 MB as float32).
- Governance: no doc restricts copying; `docs/pulse-report-provenance-map.md` calls the taxonomy and corpus WEVO IP; data-deletion template (`db-migrations/data_deletion`) deletes pulse_to_tag/pulse_benchmark rows, so a snapshot must be refreshed after deletion runs. No CODEOWNERS anywhere.

**Why:** needed to pick where Pulse keeps offline reference data for quant/tag/benchmark independence from customer-api and Artemis.
**How to apply:** scope any benchmark snapshot from Aurora, embeddings from Artemis; treat growth as ~0/week until native write-back exists. See [[wevo-prod-readonly-data-access]] and [[pulse-usage-reporting-data-map]].

set -e; mkdir -p /tmp/wevo-snap; D=~/wevo-quant-training/reference; mkdir -p $D/raw $D/log; chmod 700 ~/wevo-quant-training $D $D/raw $D/log; ls -ld ~/wevo-quant-training $D
cat > /tmp/wevo-snap/artemis_catalog.py <<'EOF'
# Runs in the artemis pod. Read-only txn against the replica (env H). Streams pulse_tag rows as JSON lines to stdout.
import os, sys, json, time, psycopg2
sql = """select id::text, name, type, is_active, deleted_at, description, created_at, updated_at, embedding::text as embedding_text,
                jsonb_typeof(embedding) as emb_type, jsonb_array_length(embedding) as emb_dim
         from wevo.pulse_tag order by type, name, id"""
kw = dict(host=os.environ['H'], port=os.environ.get('DB_PORT', 5432), dbname=os.environ['DB_NAME'], user=os.environ['DB_USER'],
          password=os.environ['DB_PASSWORD'], connect_timeout=15, application_name='quant-ref-catalog-readonly')
if os.environ.get('DB_SSLMODE'):
    kw['sslmode'] = os.environ['DB_SSLMODE']
    if kw['sslmode'] == 'verify-full':
        kw['sslrootcert'] = os.environ.get('CA_PEM_PATH', '/etc/ssl/certs/global-bundle.pem')
c = psycopg2.connect(**kw); cur = c.cursor()
cur.execute("SET default_transaction_read_only = on"); cur.execute("SET statement_timeout = '60s'"); cur.execute("SET lock_timeout = '5s'")
cur.execute("BEGIN READ ONLY")
cur.execute("SELECT pg_is_in_recovery(), current_setting('transaction_read_only'), inet_server_addr()::text, version()")
r = cur.fetchone(); print('# server in_recovery=%s ro=%s addr=%s %s' % (r[0], r[1], r[2], r[3][:40]), file=sys.stderr)
t = time.time(); cur.execute(sql); n = 0
cols = [d[0] for d in cur.description]
for row in cur:
    o = dict(zip(cols, row))
    for k in ('deleted_at', 'created_at', 'updated_at'):
        o[k] = o[k].isoformat() if o[k] is not None else None
    sys.stdout.write(json.dumps(o, ensure_ascii=False) + '\n'); n += 1
cur.execute("ROLLBACK"); c.close()
print('# rows=%d %.1fs' % (n, time.time() - t), file=sys.stderr)
EOF
echo written

        if x != 0:

    'embedding_file': 'pulse_tag_embeddings.f32',
    'embedding_layout': 'header-free, row-major, little-endian float32, shape (185, 3072)',
    'embedding_file_bytes': len(f32), 'embedding_file_sha256': sha,
    'float32_roundtrip': {'values': n_vals, 'exact': exact, 'max_abs_error': format(max_abs, 'E'), 'max_rel_error': format(max_rel, 'E'),

}
out = {'metadata': meta, 'tags': tags}
jp = os.path.join(D, 'pulse_tags.json')

print(json.dumps(meta, indent=1))
print('json bytes', os.path.getsize(jp))

#!/bin/zsh
# Off-peak Aurora export driver (Mac side). Needs: duploctl prod JIT kube creds + AWS JIT creds (both interactive to refresh).
# Loop: CPU gate (Aurora writer duplowevo-db, CloudWatch, must be <= 40%) -> one pod invocation of 10 keyset batches
# (500 result rows each, 3 s pause between batches) -> repeat until the runner reports DONE. Nothing is written in the pod.
set -u
export PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:$PATH; export AWS_PROFILE=duplo.argus.wevo.ai
D=~/wevo-quant-training/reference; OUT=$D/raw/samples_rows.jsonl; LOG=$D/log/samples_export.log; CPULOG=$D/log/cpu_aurora_writer.log
STATE=$D/log/.cursor; RUNNER=/tmp/wevo-snap/aurora_samples.js
[[ -f $RUNNER ]] || RUNNER=$D/log/aurora_samples.js
K=(kubectl --context prod -n duploservices-prod --request-timeout=600s exec -i deploy/customer-api -c customer-api --)
log() { echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) $*" | tee -a $LOG; }
cpu_now() {  # latest 1-min average CPU of the Aurora writer
  local S=$(date -u -v-6M +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) E=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --region us-east-1 --namespace AWS/RDS --metric-name CPUUtilization \
    --dimensions Name=DBInstanceIdentifier,Value=duplowevo-db --start-time $S --end-time $E --period 60 --statistics Average \
    --query "sort_by(Datapoints,&Timestamp)[-1].Average" --output text
}
gate() {
  local over=0
  while :; do
    local c=$(cpu_now); echo "$(date -u +%FT%TZ) duplowevo-db cpu=$c" >> $CPULOG
    if [[ "$c" == "None" || -z "$c" ]]; then log "CPU metric unavailable; stopping"; exit 3; fi
    if (( $(echo "$c <= 40" | bc) )); then return 0; fi
    over=$((over+1)); log "CPU $c% > 40%, pausing 60 s ($over/5)"
    (( over >= 5 )) && { log "CPU > 40% for 5 minutes; stopping"; exit 2; }
    sleep 60
  done
}
cursor=""; seq=0
if [[ -f $STATE ]]; then read cursor seq < $STATE; log "resuming from saved cursor (seq=$seq)"; fi
inv=0
log "samples export START window (local $(date))"
while :; do
  gate
  inv=$((inv+1)); tmp=$(mktemp $D/log/.stderr.XXXXXX)
  log "invocation $inv: 10 batches x 500 result rows, from seq=$seq"
  "${K[@]}" env LAST="$cursor" SEQ0=$seq BATCH=500 MAXB=10 PAUSE_MS=3000 NODE_PATH=/wevo/app/node_modules node - < $RUNNER >> $OUT 2> $tmp
  rc=$?
  grep -v '^#CURSOR' $tmp >> $LOG
  line=$(grep '^#CURSOR' $tmp | tail -1); rm -f $tmp
  if (( rc != 0 )) || [[ -z "$line" ]]; then log "invocation $inv failed rc=$rc (cursor kept for resume)"; exit 1; fi
  cursor=$(echo $line | awk '{print $2}'); seq=$(echo $line | awk '{print $3}')
  if [[ "$cursor" == "DONE" ]]; then rm -f $STATE; log "samples export DONE rows=$(wc -l < $OUT) (local $(date))"; break; fi
  (umask 077; echo "$cursor $seq" > $STATE)
  sleep 3
done
EOF

# Local post-processing: raw/samples_rows.jsonl -> samples.jsonl.gz + samples.meta.json; prints counts only.
import json, gzip, os, collections, hashlib, sys
D = os.path.expanduser('~/wevo-quant-training/reference')
src = os.path.join(D, 'raw', 'samples_rows.jsonl'); dst = os.path.join(D, 'samples.jsonl.gz')
rows = [json.loads(l) for l in open(src)]
seqs = [r['seq'] for r in rows]; assert seqs == list(range(len(rows))), 'seq not contiguous'
pulses = collections.defaultdict(set); results = set(); types = collections.Counter(); names = collections.Counter(); jt = collections.Counter()
nulls = 0
for r in rows:
    pulses[r['pulse_key']].add(r['result_key']); results.add(r['result_key']); types[r['tag_type']] += 1
    names[tuple(r['names'])] += 1
    for s in r['scores'] + [r['top_level']]:
        if s is None: nulls += 1
        else: jt[type(json.loads(s)).__name__] += 1
per_pulse_types = collections.Counter()
pt = collections.defaultdict(set)
for r in rows: pt[r['pulse_key']].add(r['tag_type'])
for k, v in pt.items(): per_pulse_types[len(v)] += 1
multi = sum(1 for v in pulses.values() if len(v) > 1)
with gzip.open(dst, 'wt', encoding='utf-8', compresslevel=9) as f:
    for r in rows: f.write(json.dumps(r, separators=(',', ':')) + '\n')
meta = {
  'snapshot_window_utc': sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None,
  'source': 'Aurora duplowevo-db (customer-api), wevo.pulse_to_tag x wevo.pulse_tag x wevo.automated_insight_session_result',
  'mirrors': 'wevo-customer-api src/data/pulseTags.js _getTagQuantData filter (ptt.deleted_at is null, aisr.quant <> {}, aisr.segment_id is null, pt.is_active); rows are BEFORE _getCombosToScores collapse',
  'row_order': 'customer-api query has no ORDER BY (order undefined there); this export is ordered by result id then pulse_to_tag id, seq is that order. The collapse keeps the LAST row per pulse.',
  'keys': 'pulse_key = sha256("pulse:" + pulse id); result_key = sha256(result id); raw ids never left the pod',
  'score_fields': 'names/scores/raw_scores are positional from quant.scores[0..2]; scores, raw_scores, top_level (quant.average), top_level_raw (quant.rawScoreAverage) are the JSON value text as stored (customer-api applies Number())',
  'rows': len(rows), 'distinct_pulses': len(pulses), 'distinct_results': len(results), 'pulses_with_multiple_results': multi,
  'rows_by_tag_type': dict(types), 'pulses_by_tag_type_count': {str(k): v for k, v in sorted(per_pulse_types.items())},
  'score_name_tuples': {','.join(k): v for k, v in names.items()}, 'score_json_types': dict(jt), 'null_score_values': nulls,
  'created_at_min': min(r['created_at'] for r in rows), 'created_at_max': max(r['created_at'] for r in rows),
  'file_sha256': hashlib.sha256(open(dst, 'rb').read()).hexdigest(), 'file_bytes': os.path.getsize(dst),
  'contains_customer_page_content': False,
}
json.dump(meta, open(os.path.join(D, 'samples.meta.json'), 'w'), indent=1)
print(json.dumps(meta, indent=1))
EOF

# Pulse tag catalog snapshot (static reference data)

Source: WEVO production Artemis database, read replica `duploartemis-prod-v2-replica`, table `wevo.pulse_tag`,
read in a read-only transaction on 2026-11-03 (20:45 UTC). This is the static 185-tag catalog
(157 product, 14 industry, 14 asset; all active, none deleted, all created 2024-08-07 and never updated).
It contains **no customer data**: only WEVO's own tag names, types, descriptions and their embeddings.

Files

- `pulse_tags.json`: `{"metadata": {...}, "tags": [...]}`. `tags` is an ordered list (ORDER BY type, name, id) of
  `embedding_row, id, name, type, is_active, deleted_at, description, created_at, updated_at`, without the embedding.
  `metadata` records the snapshot time, `embedding_dim` (3072), the embedding model (`text-embedding-3-large`),
  the layout and SHA-256 of the embedding file, and the float32 round-trip check.
- `pulse_tag_embeddings.f32`: header-free, row-major, little-endian float32, shape (185, 3072), 2,273,280 bytes.
  Row `i` is the embedding of `tags[i]` (`embedding_row == i`). The stored jsonb values were already float32-exact,
  so the round trip has zero error.

The benchmark cohort samples (per-Pulse scores) are deliberately not in git.
EOF

# Local post-processing: raw/samples_rows.jsonl (pod runner output, hashed keys) -> samples.jsonl.gz + samples.meta.json.

assert [r['seq'] for r in rows] == list(range(len(rows))), 'seq not contiguous'
def val(s):  # JSON value text as stored -> JSON value (number stays number, string stays string, null stays null)
    return None if s is None else json.loads(s)
out_rows = []; names = collections.Counter(); jt = collections.Counter(); nulls = 0

    if o['topLevel'] is None: nulls += 1
    else: jt[type(o['topLevel']).__name__] += 1
    out_rows.append(o)
pulses = collections.defaultdict(set); pt = collections.defaultdict(set); types = collections.Counter(); results = set()
for o in out_rows:
    pulses[o['pulse_key']].add(o['result_key']); pt[o['pulse_key']].add(o['tag_type']); types[o['tag_type']] += 1; results.add(o['result_key'])
with gzip.open(dst, 'wt', encoding='utf-8', compresslevel=9) as f:

meta = {
  'version': 'prod-2026-11-03',
  'snapshot_window_utc': sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else None,

  'file_sha256': hashlib.sha256(open(dst, 'rb').read()).hexdigest(), 'file_bytes': os.path.getsize(dst),
}

print(json.dumps(meta, indent=1))
EOF

# Local-quant reference bundle (`prod-2026-11-03`)

Static reference data so Pulse can run quant tagging and benchmarks without customer-api or Artemis at runtime.
Read-only snapshots of WEVO production taken on 2026-11-03. **No customer content and no raw ids**: the catalog is
WEVO's own tag taxonomy, and the samples are hashed keys plus scores.

## Files

| file | contents |
|---|---|
| `VERSION` | bundle version, one line (`prod-2026-11-03`) |
| `pulse_tags.json` | `{"metadata", "tags"}`; `tags` is the ordered 185-tag catalog without embeddings |
| `pulse_tag_embeddings.f64` | header-free, row-major, little-endian float64, shape (185, 3072), row `i` = `tags[i]` |
| `samples.jsonl.gz` | frozen benchmark cohort, pre-collapse rows (see below) |

## Tag catalog

Source: Artemis production **read replica** `duploartemis-prod-v2-replica`, table `wevo.pulse_tag`, all rows,
read in a read-only transaction at 2026-11-03 20:45 UTC.

- 185 tags: 157 product, 14 industry, 14 asset. All active, none deleted, all created 2024-08-07, never updated.
- Each tag: `embedding_row, id, name, type, is_active, deleted_at, description, created_at, updated_at`.
  Order is `ORDER BY type, name, id`; `embedding_row` is the row index into the `.f64` file.
- Embeddings: `text-embedding-3-large`, 3072 dims, stored in Artemis as jsonb number arrays. They are written as
  float64 (`metadata.embedding_dim`, `embedding_file_sha256`). Round-trip check: every one of the 568,320 values
  parses back to exactly the stored decimal text (max abs error 0).

## Benchmark cohort samples

Source: Aurora `duplowevo-db` (the customer-api database), the same join customer-api uses to build its in-process
benchmark cache. Exported off-peak in keyset batches (500 result rows, 3 s pause, CloudWatch CPU gate), read-only.

The filter mirrors `_getTagQuantData` in `wevo-customer-api/src/data/pulseTags.js` exactly:

```sql
from wevo.pulse_to_tag ptt
join wevo.pulse_tag pt on pt.id = ptt.tag_id
join wevo.automated_insight_session_result aisr on aisr.automated_insight_session_id = ptt.pulse_id
where ptt.deleted_at is null          -- undeleted pulse_to_tag
  and aisr.quant <> '{}'              -- non-empty quant
  and aisr.segment_id is null         -- top-level result, not a segment
  and pt.is_active is true            -- active tag
-- created_at is the RESULT's created_at (aisr.created_at), not the session's
```

One row per (pulse_to_tag, result) pair, **before** customer-api's JS collapse (`_getCombosToScores`), so Pulse can
reproduce that step. Note the collapse keeps the last row seen per pulse; the customer-api query has no `ORDER BY`,
so its order is undefined. This file is ordered by result id, then pulse_to_tag id, and the line order is the order
the export SQL returned.

Row: `{pulse_key, result_key, created_at, Intuitive, Trusted, Valuable, topLevel, tag_id, tag_type}`

- `pulse_key` = sha256 hex of the string `"pulse:" + <pulse id>`; `result_key` = sha256 hex of `<result id>`.
  Raw ids were hashed inside the database pod and never left it.
- `Intuitive`/`Trusted`/`Valuable` = `quant.scores[].score` matched by `quant.scores[].name`, value as stored
  (customer-api applies `Number()` to it); `topLevel` = `quant.average` as stored.
- `created_at` = `aisr.created_at` (ISO 8601 UTC).
- `tag_id` / `tag_type` = the pulse_tag row (`type` is `product`, `industry` or `asset`).

Counts: see `samples.meta.json` next to the raw export; summary is filled in below once the off-peak export has run.

SAMPLES_COUNTS_PLACEHOLDER
EOF

content.text:
Catalog is done and on the branch; the samples export is fully prepared but could not be run yet. Details below.

**Status**

- The tag catalog is exported, verified, and committed. The benchmark cohort samples are **not yet exported**. Ryan's rule requires a US-night window, and no credential on this machine survives until then: the prod kube token from `duploctl jit` and the `duplo.argus.wevo.ai` AWS token are both one-hour JIT tokens that refresh only through a browser login. An unattended night run is impossible. Someone must log in at window start and run two commands (below).

**Catalog (done, from the Artemis read replica)**

- Query ran 2026-11-03 20:45:11 to 20:45:18 UTC inside a `BEGIN READ ONLY` transaction with `default_transaction_read_only=on`, `statement_timeout=60s`, `lock_timeout=5s`; the server reported `pg_is_in_recovery=true` (replica confirmed). Query time 0.5 s, 185 rows.

```sql
select id::text, name, type, is_active, deleted_at, description, created_at, updated_at,
       embedding::text as embedding_text, jsonb_typeof(embedding), jsonb_array_length(embedding)
from wevo.pulse_tag order by type, name, id
```

- Replica CPU was 4 to 7 percent before and during the export. CloudWatch then shows 32 percent at 15:46 and 51 percent at 15:47 EST, back to 7 percent by 15:49. That spike started about a minute after my 7-second export finished, and a similar 33 percent spike appears at 15:17 before I ran anything, so I believe it is unrelated, but I cannot prove it from the metric alone.

| item | value |
|---|---|
| tags | 185 (product 157, industry 14, asset 14), all active, none deleted |
| embedding | 3072 dims, all rows |
| pulse_tags.json | 285,565 bytes |
| pulse_tag_embeddings.f64 | 4,546,560 bytes, sha256 540fbfbc… |
| float64 round trip | 568,320 values, 568,320 exact, max abs error 0 |

- Round-trip method: each jsonb number's decimal text was parsed as `Decimal`, written as a little-endian double, read back, and its shortest repr compared to the stored text. Every value matched. An independent check also compared the exact binary expansion of each double to the stored text: max difference 1.3e-17, which is just decimal-versus-binary representation of the same double. No values were printed.

**Branch**

- `wevo-pulse` branch `local-quant-reference-catalog`, based on `origin/feat/local-quant-tags-benchmarks` (c29c49c14), pushed to origin. One commit `a0f7b47f4` with the requested bundle message, containing `README.md`, `VERSION` (`prod-2026-11-03`), `pulse_tags.json`, `pulse_tag_embeddings.f64` under `backend/app/services/local_quant/reference/`. The earlier float32 commit was replaced by a force-push (the branch was minutes old and had no PR). The README already documents the samples format, the exact cohort filter, the hashing, and the row-order note, with one placeholder line for the counts. The commit was made with hooks bypassed, so no Entire checkpoint was captured for it.

**Samples export (prepared, EXPLAIN'd, smoke-tested, not run)**

- Pod runner `/tmp/wevo-snap/aurora_samples.js` runs in the customer-api pod, hashes ids inside the pod, and sets the three read-only session settings. Keyset is on the result primary key:

```sql
with r as (
  select aisr.id, aisr.automated_insight_session_id as pulse_id, aisr.created_at,
         aisr.quant->'scores'->0->>'name', (aisr.quant->'scores'->0->'score')::text, (aisr.quant->'scores'->0->'rawScore')::text,
         ... same for ->1 and ->2 ...,
         (aisr.quant->'average')::text, (aisr.quant->'rawScoreAverage')::text
  from wevo.automated_insight_session_result aisr
  where aisr.id > $1::uuid and aisr.segment_id is null and aisr.quant <> '{}'
    and exists (select 1 from wevo.pulse_to_tag x join wevo.pulse_tag y on y.id = x.tag_id
                where x.pulse_id = aisr.automated_insight_session_id and x.deleted_at is null and y.is_active is true)
  order by aisr.id limit $2)
select r.id, r.pulse_id, t.tag_id, t.tag_type, r.created_at, ...scores...
from r cross join lateral (
  select pt.id as tag_id, pt.type as tag_type, ptt.id as ptt_id
```

Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject.
